text.p: The Turkish lira eased to 92,075 against the dollar on Wednesday from 91,850 at Tuesday's close on banks' dollar demand and central bank's higher dollar rate for banks' forex transfers, bankers said.
The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory currency transfers at 92,000 lira at the opening, up from 91,800 at Tuesday's close. Later, it decreased the rate to 91,950 lira.
Bankers said the banks' dollar demand was relatively high due to the higher liquidity.
The o/n money traded between 63 and 74.75 percent during the day and the central bank injected 12.6 trillion lira at 75 percent at close.

The central bank had injected a total of 35.95 trillion lira by buying seven-day repos and by overnight lending at 75 percent on Tuesday. In the last 15 days, o/n rate has stayed just below the central bank's offer rate 75 percent.
T-bill yields fell by one-to-two points on higher liquidity.
The average yield on the most heavily traded March 26 paper eased to 126.31 percent from 127.97 on Tuesday.
The second most active May 7 paper, which was sold at 131.20 percent average rate at yesterday's auction, yielded 128.67 percent average. -- Istanbul Newsroom, +90-212-275 0875
